statement: For independent cap-one X,Y,Z and nonzero a,b, Q=2aXY+bZ^2 has a continuous density with sup norm at most 4/sqrt(|ab|). Thus the exact physical matrix [[0,a,0],[a,0,0],[0,0,b]] has density bound 4 whenever |a|,|b|>=1; the same bound survives arbitrary affine terms and therefore arbitrary outside conditioning when this is a physical principal block.
proof_premises: Exact density formula for bZ^2 in the original physical coordinate: k_b(w)<=(b w)^(-1/2) after output reflection to b>0.
One-dimensional bathtub/layer-cake maximization for a decreasing one-sided u^(-1/2) kernel under density cap one and mass one.
Second bathtub maximization of integral f_Y(y)|y|^(-1/2)dy by the centered unit interval.
L1 convolution continuity plus dominated convergence using the integrable |y|^(-1/2) envelope.
Translations preserve original-coordinate independence and density caps.

partner_result_applied.application: Combined with the new null-pair theorem to give sup over the union of the aligned-majority Gaussian-completion branch and exact complementary-null branch <= max(C_maj,4)=C_maj<3sqrt(2).

unpaid_implication: No reduction from an arbitrary three-large-eigenvalue physical matrix to this exact null-pair principal block is proved. General non-null, non-collinear multi-heavy-row coupling remains open; full QFORM remains open.
next_step: Attack the smallest exact three-heavy non-null/non-collinear physical family not reducible by translations to 2aXY+bZ^2; preserve product provenance and seek a global-output bound or source-valid counterexample.
